target_customer: Originally households wanting ongoing in-home tech support; later small businesses, startups and corporate IT teams needing on-site hands
problem: Connected devices and office tech break or need setup and people lack trusted on-demand help.
business_model: Subscription tech support, later on-demand on-site IT services

founders.name: Colin Barceloux
previous_startups: Axius (venture-backed smart home device management, went through StartX)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; later CEO of Lively Root.

founders.name: Scott Hasbrouck
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and CTO, no bio.

competitors.name: HelloTech and Geekatoo
competitors.what: Merged on-demand in-home tech support network

competitors.name: Eden
competitors.what: YC S15 on-demand tech pros for electronics help and installation
competitors.funding_then: About 2 million dollars raised in 2015 per TechCrunch headline

competitors.name: Geek Squad
competitors.what: Best Buy incumbent with home visits tied to subscription plans

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly a dispatch and services marketplace with remote support tools, not deep technology.

defensibility.rationale: Services business with many similar competitors; the vetted technician network gave limited lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent and rivals consolidated in 2016 (HelloTech and Geekatoo merged); Techmate's own outcome is unclear.

market_need_then: Demo Day coverage (TechCrunch, August 2016) reported about 30K dollars monthly revenue growing 25 percent weekly, which indicates early demand for home tech help.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simple, transparent and fast booking per YC page

brand_strength.rationale: Generic compound name with several unrelated TECHMATE trademarks held by other owners; no source shows brand press or community.

pivots.from: Subscription in-home tech support for households (YC blog 2016)
pivots.to: On-demand on-site IT support for small businesses and corporate IT teams
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; direction shown by the YC page and current site

outcome_analysis: Techmate launched in YC Summer 2016 as home tech support, reported about 30K dollars monthly revenue at Demo Day, then moved toward business IT support. Its site and a 2024 press release show Techmate Technologies still operating in 2025 with a large technician network, which conflicts with the YC listing of Acquired; no acquirer was found. The cause or form of any exit is not public in what was found.
notes: YC marks Acquired but no acquisition evidence found and the site shows an active company with a 2025 copyright; exit recorded unknown. Aggregators list a 2016-08 seed with YC, StartX and others and 5.9M over 7 rounds (CB Insights), but no round has a second source so none is recorded. A ChannelE2E item says Barceloux also leads marketing at Domotz; its cited CEO name David Brock is unverified. Founding year from YC page. Update: the 2016-08 seed (Seedtable) is now recorded as a round with amount null; it rests on a single database. Seedtable also shows a 2020-07 seed of $1.0M, CB Insights shows $5.9M over 7 rounds with $1.98M in 2022-05, and KingsCrowd lists a Techmate under different founders, so those are not recorded as they may belong to a different company.
